name: Dig Tsho, Khumbu, Nepal (1985) — wave-triggered breach chain

sources.citation: Vuichard, D. & Zimmermann, M. (1987), as reported in Bajracharya, Shrestha & Rajbhandari, 'Glacial Lake Outburst Floods in the Sagarmatha Region', Mountain Research and Development 27(4)
Cenderelli & Wohl-type peak discharge compilation, 'Peak discharge estimates of glacial-lake outburst floods and normal climatic floods in the Mount Everest region, Nepal'

Westoby, M.J. et al. (2014), 'Modelling outburst floods from moraine-dammed glacial lakes', Earth-Science Reviews 134 — moraine breach erodibility is calibrated, not measured, and the trigger is a displacement wave over near-zero freeboard.

sourced.volumeM3: ~5,000,000 m3 of water released (Bajracharya et al. 2007)
sourced.initialWL: lake believed full to its rim just before the outbreak (Bajracharya et al. 2007) — freeboard 0, modeled as level with the crest
sourced.surfaceAreaHa: Dig Tsho lake area ~0.5 km2 = 50 ha (Sagarmatha-region GLOF inventories)
sourced.waveOvertopDepth: peak crest-overtopping depth d0 = 3.93 m from the Impulse module's 3D run-up of the representative displacement wave (R = 8.73 m, freeboard 0) — the ice-avalanche surge that triggered this event
sourced.waveOvertopDuration: overtopping duration tO = 41.7 s from the same 3D run-up result

modelingNotes.activeWaterColumn: crestElev is set to the ~18 m ACTIVE WATER COLUMN (lake depth at the dam), NOT the ~60 m moraine dam height used in the seed case dig-tsho-1985.json. 5.0M m3 over ~50 ha gives a mean depth ~10 m and a max depth ~18 m; the breach cuts through the moraine down to the lake floor (baseElev 0). Using the full 60 m as the water column makes the headcut-breakthrough invert drop (crestElev - 0.15*Hb = 9 m) fire an unphysical instantaneous discharge spike at t ~ 36 s.
modelingNotes.waveIsTheTrigger: With freeboard 0 and inflowM3s 0, the standing head is zero and the dam does NOT breach without the wave (Qpeak = 0.0, the documented -100% failure). The wave-overtopping pulse train supplies the transient erosive head that initiates crest incision; once the invert cuts below still-water level the lake self-drains. Set waveForcingEnabled=false to recover the 0.0 result.
modelingNotes.calibratedErodibility: erosionIndexI = 1.17 is CALIBRATED (a highly erodible loose bouldery till), not sourced — no measured Dig Tsho till erodibility exists. This follows standard moraine-breach back-analysis practice (Westoby et al. 2014): the wave-forcing chain enables initiation, then erodibility is the single knob tuned to the observed peak. The energy-headcut coefficient C, wave count, and deepening-gate fraction have only second-order effect on Qpeak.
modelingNotes.headcutLaw: headcutLaw='energy' uses the WinDAM/USDA-SITES energy-dissipation migration dX/dt = C*(q*H)^(1/3); the legacy hydrostatic law gives a similar peak here because the peak is drawdown/erodibility-governed once the crest is cut through.

unsourcedFieldsNote: Moraine geometry and till erodibility remain unsourced/calibrated. This case demonstrates the wave->breach forcing chain (Improvement #2) reproducing the observed peak; it is a calibrated back-analysis, not a blind prediction. Breach WIDTH is over-predicted (~105 m simulated vs field estimates nearer ~60 m) — a known limitation of the smooth-widening + screening bank-collapse proxy, pending the Culmann limit-equilibrium upgrade (Improvement #3).

peakDischargeM3s.note: 1600 m3/s reported at/near the breach site (Vuichard & Zimmermann 1987, via Bajracharya et al. 2007). A separate compilation reports ~1375 m3/s at a gauge 7.1 km downstream — the two aren't directly comparable (different measurement points) but both are included as the genuine range across sources rather than picking one.
peakDischargeM3s.source: Vuichard & Zimmermann 1987; Cenderelli-type peak discharge compilation

breachFormationHours.note: No sourced breach-formation duration found yet for this event. The simulated peak arrives ~0.8 h after the wave trigger; treat as a model output, not an observation.
